newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to Nafta shares push Slovak SAX index higher.
newsitem.headline: Gains to Nafta shares push Slovak SAX index higher.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with strong gains to Nafta pushing the Slovak SAX index up 1.5 points to 200.25.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta rose 175 crowns to 1,925, on volume of 10,002 shares traded, with brokers predicting continued interest in the issue.

"We see both domestic and foreign investors interested in Nafta at the current price," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said. "It is still hard to forecast further movements (of Nafta's price), but I see further growth potential in this share."
Sykora added that interest in VSZ steel also was strengthening, as the issue enters an upward curve in its trading cycle. VSZ closed up 10 crowns at 630.
The largest issue on the BSE, oil refiner Slovnaft, closed up 15 crowns at 945, but its average price was 0.53 percent lower.
Overall volume increased to 384,057 shares, from 259,591 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover rose to 263.14 million crowns, from 151.86 million.
